## CEO BRIEFING

**For Dana Whitfield — board call at 15:00 UTC. Prepared 14:20 UTC, incident INC-2026-1109-01. All times UTC.**

**What happened**
- At 11:42 the Batch API began returning elevated errors (502s) on job submissions. The problem was confined to one of our two Batch worker fleets; the Inference, Embeddings and Files APIs were unaffected throughout.
- At 12:58 we mitigated by moving all Batch API traffic to the healthy fleet. Error rates fell to near the 0.2% baseline within two minutes and have held there (0.3% as of 14:12).
- Root cause is **not established**. Two hypotheses remain live and untested: this morning's 11:31 release (it lowered the workers' database connection-pool ceiling from 80 to 24), and a large load spike from 11:38. They may interact. The upstream storage provider has been ruled out. Nothing is confirmed — the earlier status-page claim that a cause was identified was published in error and is being corrected now.
- Our policy requires 90 minutes of continuous normal error rate before we may declare resolution. That verification window runs to **14:30**. As of 14:20 the incident is mitigated, not resolved.

**Who is hit**
- Batch API only, between 11:42 and 12:58. **17,602 of 58,900 Batch API requests failed — 29.9%.** That is about 2% of the 842,000 requests we served across all APIs in the window.
- **7 of our 9 Batch API accounts** were affected, each losing roughly a third of its Batch traffic in the window: stark-industries, contoso, wayne-enterprises, globex, wonka-industries, umbrella-health, initech. The other two Batch accounts and all non-Batch traffic were unaffected.
- Failed jobs are being re-driven: ~60% complete at 13:52, no failures on replay. Five support tickets today from four affected accounts (Contoso ×2, Umbrella Health, Wonka Industries, Globex).

**Commercial exposure**
- Contoso is the **only** affected account on a contract carrying service credits (Schedule B: 99.9% monthly availability; 10/25/50% credit tiers). The other six are on standard terms with no credit clause.
- Monthly availability is determined after month end and published within 10 business days; Contoso's claim window only opens after publication. **Nothing to quantify or accrue today.** Contoso asked about credits at 12:26; I am replying to them now with their own figures (9,400 requests, 3,410 failures) and the determination timeline.
- Schedule B does allow exclusions for customer-caused failures; any exclusion must be published with volume and basis.

**Where things will stand at 15:00**
- The verification window closes at 14:30. I will message you the outcome between 14:30 and 14:45, before your call.
- Engineering's internal planning estimate is full wrap-up around 16:00 **if** the window closes clean and the replay finishes. That is an internal estimate only — do not quote it externally.
- A corrective status-page update is publishing at 14:20 (see below).

**If it comes up — safe to say:** "Between 11:42 and 12:58 UTC we had elevated errors on our Batch API; about 30% of Batch requests in that window failed. We mitigated by moving traffic to healthy infrastructure within 76 minutes, error rates are back to normal, and we are replaying affected customers' failed jobs. Our other APIs were unaffected. We're in a standard 90-minute verification window closing at 14:30 UTC and will confirm recovery after that. Root cause is under investigation. Updates are on the status page."

**Do not say:** any statement of cause (including "identified"); a resolution or restoration time; internal fleet architecture; Contoso contract specifics beyond "credits are determined monthly under the contract." If the window does not close clean, the line is: "the mitigation is holding and verification is continuing."

## ENGINEERING UPDATE

**INC-2026-1109-01 — handoff at 14:20 UTC. All times UTC.**

**Current state**
- Mitigated 12:58: all Batch traffic cut over to fleet-b; fleet-a drained and out of rotation. `POST /v1/batch/jobs` at 0.3% at 14:12 vs 0.2% baseline. Queue depth normal. Verification window closes **14:30** (10 minutes). Reminder from 13:01: mitigated, not fixed — no "resolved" language anywhere until the window closes clean.
- Re-drive of failed jobs ~60% at 13:52, no failures.
- Root cause open. H1: r3 pool change 80→24 (leading — shipped 11:31, workers observably queueing on DB connections; but r3 also runs clean on fleet-b). H2: concentrated load, ~3x morning average from 11:38 (against: fleet-a took a higher peak on 11-03). H3: storage provider — rejected 11:47. H1/H2 and their interaction are all untested.

**Impact figures** (computed from `customer-impact.csv`; the log deliberately carries no aggregate)

| Account | Requests in window | Failures |
|---|---|---|
| stark-industries | 14,200 | 5,180 |
| contoso | 9,400 | 3,410 |
| wayne-enterprises | 7,850 | 2,790 |
| globex | 6,100 | 2,240 |
| wonka-industries | 5,900 | 2,020 |
| umbrella-health | 4,300 | 1,560 |
| initech | 1,150 | 402 |
| **Total (9 Batch accounts)** | **58,900** | **17,602 (29.9%)** |

acme-corp and aperture-labs (fleet-b) had zero failures. External reporting basis is Batch-wide, never per-fleet — fleet membership stays internal.

**Immediate (next 15 minutes)**
- 14:30: close the verification window. Before declaring resolution, confirm explicitly that 0.3–0.4% against a 0.2% baseline satisfies the policy's "normal error rate" — Marcus + IC call at close. I'll post the outcome in-channel by ~14:35.
- Finish the re-drive (remaining ~40% as of 13:52) — Priya. Report completion in-channel.

**Root cause (after the window closes)**
- Marcus to propose a rollback test on fleet-a that separates H1 from H2. fleet-a now serves no customer traffic, so testing can be done without customer exposure; design it so the degraded state is captured before anything is changed (the 12:31 concern). Address the H1×H2 interaction explicitly.
- fleet-a returns to rotation only once the cause is understood. Before then, check fleet-b headroom now that it carries 100% of Batch traffic.

**Comms — so nobody is surprised**
- 14:20: corrective status-page update publishing. It retracts the 12:05 "cause identified" claim (wrong, per Marcus at 12:09), states mitigation/monitoring, and promises the next update by 14:45. Nothing about cause goes external until Marcus confirms.
- Contoso email going out now: their own figures plus the Schedule B determination timeline (answers TKT-8903/8907).
- Support (Tomas): globex (TKT-8918) — yes, affected; reply with their own figures. wonka (TKT-8912) — replay in progress, no resubmit needed. umbrella-health (TKT-8904) has a compliance export due today — prioritise their replay and reply.
- All external statements come from Tomas/Ruth off the approved list only.

**Separate, CONFIDENTIAL — staff only, not for the board or any external channel**
- SEC-411: the batch worker's database role holds unneeded write access to the billing schema. Unrelated to this incident and not a contributing factor. Marcus owns it; narrow to read-only this week.

## CUSTOMER EMAIL

To: Contoso Ltd — reply on tickets TKT-8903 / TKT-8907
Subject: Batch API incident today — your account impact and your Schedule B question

Dear Contoso team,

Thank you for your messages today (TKT-8903 and TKT-8907), and I am sorry for the disruption to your batch workflows this morning.

**What happened, and your figures.** Between 11:42 and 12:58 UTC we saw elevated error rates on the Batch API. Your account was affected: of the 9,400 Batch API requests you made in that window, 3,410 returned errors (502 responses on batch job submissions) — about 36% of your Batch traffic in the window. Your first failure was recorded at 11:43 UTC and your last at 12:56 UTC. We have no record of any further failed submissions on your account since 12:56 UTC.

At 12:58 UTC we applied a mitigation that moved Batch API traffic to healthy infrastructure; error rates returned to near-normal levels within minutes. We are monitoring the service before confirming recovery. Failed job submissions from the incident window are being re-driven on our side — roughly 60% of the backlog across affected accounts had been replayed as of 13:52 UTC, with no failures on replay — so you do not need to resubmit anything. Only the Batch API was affected; your Inference and Files API traffic was unaffected.

**Your Schedule B question.** We are not able to confirm today whether November will fall below the 99.9% commitment or what credit, if any, would apply. Monthly Availability is calculated across the calendar month and is determined by Northstar from its own service records after the end of the month, with the figure published within 10 business days of month end (B.5). The window described above will be assessed as part of that calculation, alongside the rest of the month, using the Eligible Requests definition in B.2. If any requests are excluded from Eligible Requests, we will identify the excluded volume and the basis for the exclusion in the published figure, and you may dispute an exclusion within the claim window (B.6). If the published figure falls below the commitment, you may submit a credit claim within 30 days of publication.

I will write to you again by 14:45 UTC with the current state. Your ops lead, Priya Raghunathan, is very welcome to engage with us directly on this thread.

Separately, and unrelated to today's incident: our 4 November note (TKT-8841) flagged that your integration retries failed submissions immediately with no backoff, which can trip your contracted rate limits. When your Q4 freeze lifts, deploying the backoff change you have written will help — particularly during busy periods.

Kind regards,
Incident Commander, Northstar Technologies (INC-2026-1109-01)

## STATUS PAGE UPDATE

## 2026-11-09 14:20 — Monitoring

Elevated error rates on the Batch API began at 11:42 UTC. At 12:58 UTC we applied a mitigation, moving all Batch API traffic to healthy infrastructure. Error rates returned to near-normal levels within minutes and have remained there. We are continuing to monitor the service before confirming recovery.

A correction to our earlier update: our 12:05 update stated that the cause of this incident had been identified. That was incorrect — no cause has yet been confirmed, and our investigation is continuing.

Failed job submissions from the incident window are being re-driven for affected accounts; customers do not need to resubmit them.

This incident affects the Batch API only. Other Northstar APIs are unaffected.

We will post our next update by 14:45 UTC.
